## Preliminaries

**Working scope (declared as assumption, not fact).** Mic 1:1-16 is taken as a single reading unit — the book's opening oracle: superscription (v1) → universal courtroom summons and theophany (vv2-4) → charge and verdict against Samaria (vv5-7) → the prophet's own lament (v8) → the wound's spread to Judah/Jerusalem (v9) → a wordplay lament-oracle over a chain of Judahite towns (vv10-16). "Bearing on the inner being" here is taken to include: (i) Micah himself (v1, v8 — the chapter's only human individual given explicit, vivid stated interior content); (ii) the LORD (vv2-4, 6-7, 9, 12 — the book's controlling divine voice and operative agent, in scope per note (b) as the operation grounding every human judgment that follows); (iii) "the peoples"/"the earth and all in it" (v2, a maximal collective addressed as both summoned witness-audience and, per an open question below, possibly the very party being witnessed against); (iv) Jacob/the house of Israel and Judah (v5, the named guilty collectives); (v) Samaria, personified as an unfaithful woman (v7); (vi) each named town's "inhabitants" (vv10-15, a chain of distinct human collectives, each individually charged); (vii) the addressed mother-city (vv13, 16, personified, grieving for exiled children).

**Reading rule applied.** No [AMBIGUOUS]-span STEP-live resolution was needed — the base extract reports 100% meaning coverage for this range (187/187 non-particle spans). Hebrew prophetic judgment-oracle register throughout, shifting registers within the chapter: third-person narrative superscription (v1), divine imperative summons (v2), theophanic description (vv3-4), rhetorical question-and-answer (v5), divine first-person judgment (vv6-7), prophetic first-person lament (v8), narrated report (v9), then a distinct sub-genre — a chain of paronomasia (name-wordplay) laments addressed in turn to named towns (vv10-16), imperative/jussive mood throughout.

**Corpus-continuity check.** No prior filled debate found for this book at or before this range — this is the first debate in the sequence (or nothing precedes it yet). Nothing to re-read.

## Per-verse debate

### Mic 1:1

> The word of the Lord that came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.

**Observation.** "The word [H1697G] of the LORD [H3068G] that came [H1961] to Micah [H4318K] of Moresheth [H4183], in the days [H3117G] of Jotham [H3147H], Ahaz [H0271G], and Hezekiah [H3169H], kings [H4428G] of Judah [H3063G], which [H0834A] he saw [H2372] concerning [H5921A] Samaria [H8111] and Jerusalem [H3389]."

**Operation 1 — the word of the LORD coming to be Micah's own.**
- **Action-type:** came/was (a book's own opening formula, matching the pattern already established at Joel 1:1/Jonah 1:1/Obad 1).
- **Subject:** Micah — named as the word's recipient; the verb itself (H1961, "to be") is bare copula, stating only that the word simply "was" Micah's, not describing his own reception.
- **Operation:** a state — the word "is" Micah's; no response or reaction is described at this point.
- **Source:** the LORD, explicit.
- **Target:** n/a directly; the word's own content (Samaria and Jerusalem) is the object of Operation 2.

**Operation 2 — Micah's own seeing of the vision.**
- **Action-type:** saw (a genuinely stated cognitive/visionary act, distinct from Operation 1's bare reception).
- **Subject:** Micah — this time given an active verb of his own, "which he saw" (H2372, chazah — the same root used elsewhere in the prophetic corpus for ecstatic/prophetic seeing, not ordinary sight).
- **Operation:** a state/movement — the perceiving of a prophetic vision.
- **Source:** self, exercising the visionary capacity; ultimately enabled by the word's coming (Operation 1), though the text keeps the two distinct — reception (state) then seeing (act), Part B.5's state-vs-enablement distinction directly relevant.
- **Target:** "concerning Samaria and Jerusalem" — the vision's own content, the two cities that will structure the whole chapter (Samaria: vv2-9; Jerusalem/Judah's towns: vv9-16).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Micah — a focused inner being in his own right from the book's first verse, given an explicit act (seeing) rather than only being named. The named kings (Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah) are not candidates here — no operation, state, or act is attributed to them; they function solely as a chronological anchor, correctly set aside per step 3 note (a).
- Q3: Both the word's coming and Micah's seeing are stated explicitly, not inferred.
- Q4: Source of the word = the LORD, explicit. Source of the seeing = Micah's own faculty, exercised once the word had come — the two kept distinct rather than collapsed into one.
- Q5: Target = "Samaria and Jerusalem," the vision's own named content.
- Q6: State (the word's bare coming) and movement/act (the seeing).
- Q7: Forward linkage to the whole chapter — Samaria (vv2-9) and Jerusalem/Judah (vv9-16) are named here as the vision's twin objects, structuring everything that follows.
- Q8: N/A this verse — Micah addressed as an individual.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; nothing about Micah's own interior response to receiving/seeing the vision is given here (that comes explicitly at v8).
- Q11: came/was (the word's reception); saw (Micah's own act).

**Decision.** Retain both operations. The kings are set aside (no operation stated); Micah's own two-part reception-then-seeing is retained as the book's own formal opening.

### Mic 1:2

> Hear, you peoples, all of you; pay attention, O earth, and all that is in it, and let the Lord God be a witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.

**Observation.** "Hear [H8085G], you peoples [H5971A], all [H3605] of you; pay attention [H7181], O earth [H0776G], and all the fullness [H4393] of it; and let the Lord [H0136] GOD [H3069] be a witness [H5707] against you, the LORD [H0136] from his holy [H6944G] temple [H1964G]."

**Operation 1 — the universal summons to hear.**
- **Action-type:** summoned/commanded (an imperative address to the widest possible human audience).
- **Subject:** "you peoples, all of you" — a maximal human collective (note (c)), addressed directly; "the earth, and all that is in it" — a non-human totality named alongside it, in scope per note (b) as the setting/audience the human peoples are embedded in.
- **Operation:** a movement — a command to attend, directed outward at the widest possible scope.
- **Source:** the LORD/the prophet's own voice, speaking with divine authority (unattributed grammatically within this clause, continuing v1's frame).
- **Target:** "the peoples," "the earth" — the summons's own addressees.

**Operation 2 — the Lord GOD's self-declared witness against "you."**
- **Action-type:** witnessed (a divine self-appointment as accuser/witness).
- **Subject:** the Lord GOD (H0136/H3069), "the LORD from his holy temple" — the book's controlling divine voice.
- **Operation:** a state — a declared legal role, witness-against, framed within courtroom (rib-controversy) imagery.
- **Source:** self — the LORD's own declared intention.
- **Target:** "you" (2mp) — grammatically the same "peoples" just summoned as the audience in Operation 1, raising a genuine interpretive question (below): are the summoned peoples the audience of a witness against SOMEONE ELSE not yet named, or are they themselves the accused, addressed in the same breath as both audience and defendant?

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "The peoples" — a focused collective, given an explicit summons; their own interior (compliance, resistance, indifference) is not stated, only the command itself.
- Q3: Both operations stated explicitly, via direct imperative and direct declaration.
- Q4: Source of the summons and the witness-declaration = the LORD/prophetic voice, self, explicit.
- Q5: Target = "the peoples"/"the earth" (Operation 1); "you" (Operation 2) — genuinely ambiguous whether this "you" is identical to the peoples just summoned or a distinct, not-yet-named party (Samaria/Jerusalem, named only from v5) — named as an open interpretive fork, not resolved here, per Part B.9.
- Q6: Movement (the summons) and state (the declared witness-role).
- Q7: Forward linkage — this verse's unresolved "you" is most plausibly resolved retrospectively once Samaria and Judah are named as the guilty parties at v5; the courtroom framing here anticipates the verdict pronounced at vv6-7.
- Q8: "The peoples, all of you" and "the earth, and all that is in it" — both maximal collectives, addressed together as one universal audience.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the identity of "you" in "witness against you" is not resolved within this verse — named as insufficiency/interpretive fork.
- Q11: summoned (the peoples); witnessed (the LORD, self-declared).

**Decision.** Retain both operations. The dual role of "you" (summoned audience vs. accused) is carried forward as an interpretive fork per Part B.9, not settled here.

### Mic 1:3

> For behold, the Lord is coming out of his place, and will come down and tread upon the high places of the earth.

**Observation.** "For behold [H2009], the LORD [H3068G] is coming out [H3318G] of his place [H4725], and will come down [H3381] and tread [H1869] upon the high places [H1116] of the earth [H0776G]."

**Operation 1 — the LORD's theophanic descent.**
- **Action-type:** came-out/came-down/trod (a three-part theophanic movement, the direct enactment of v2's declared witness-role).
- **Subject:** the LORD (non-human, in scope per note (b) as the book's controlling divine operative agent).
- **Operation:** a movement — leaving his own place, descending, and treading upon the earth's high places (elevated ground, often cultic/idolatrous sites elsewhere in the corpus).
- **Source:** self — the LORD's own stated action, no external cause.
- **Target:** "the high places of the earth" — a non-human, geographic/cultic object, not yet a named human party.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: No human party is named in this verse; per step 2 note (d) a verse with only a non-human being would be set aside UNLESS that non-human's operation bears on a human in the passage's own context — here it plainly does, as the direct, immediate enactment of the courtroom scene opened at v2 and the ground for the verdict named at v5-6; retained on that basis, not set aside.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, introduced by "behold" (H2009), marking it as vivid, certain, imminent.
- Q4: Source = the LORD, self, explicit.
- Q5: Target = "the high places of the earth" — non-human, geographic.
- Q6: Movement throughout (coming out, coming down, treading).
- Q7: Direct forward linkage to v4 (the physical consequence of this descent) and to v5-6 (its stated cause and specific human target, Samaria).
- Q8: N/A this verse — no human collective is addressed.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: came-out/came-down/trod.

**Decision.** Retain — the passage's central theophanic operation, grounding every human verdict that follows; no human bearing directly within THIS verse, but retained per note (d)'s own exception (the operation's bearing on humans is supplied by the immediate passage context, not this verse alone).

### Mic 1:4

> And the mountains will melt under him, and the valleys will split open, like wax before the fire, like waters poured down a steep place.

**Observation.** "And the mountains [H2022G] will melt [H4549] under [H8478G] him, and the valleys [H6010R] will split open [H1234], like wax [H1749] before [H6440G] the fire [H0784], like waters [H4325G] poured down [H5064] a steep place [H4174]."

**Operation 1 — the cosmic dissolution accompanying the LORD's descent.**
- **Action-type:** melted/split (a continuation and physical consequence of v3's theophany).
- **Subject:** "the mountains," "the valleys" — non-human, entirely physical; no human party named or implied within this verse.
- **Operation:** a movement — melting like wax, splitting like water poured down a slope, similes underscoring total, effortless dissolution before the LORD's presence.
- **Source:** the LORD's presence/descent (v3), continuing directly, not restated as an explicit subject within this verse's own grammar.
- **Target:** n/a directly (the mountains/valleys are themselves the ones acted upon, not acting on a further target).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: No human candidate present. Per step 2 note (d), a verse with ONLY non-human content whose bearing on a human is not related "in the context of the passage" is out of scope — here the mountains/valleys carry no independent human bearing of their own beyond continuing v3's theophany; retained only as the direct physical continuation of v3 (already justified there), not as an independently human-bearing verse in its own right.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, via direct simile.
- Q4: Source = the LORD's presence, continuing from v3, not restated.
- Q5: N/A directly — the mountains/valleys are the objects dissolving, not impacting a further target within this verse.
- Q6: Movement (melting, splitting).
- Q7: Direct continuation of v3; together vv3-4 form one theophanic unit.
- Q8: N/A.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: melted/split (continuing v3's came-down/trod).

**Decision.** Set aside as an independent IB operation (no human bearing of its own within this verse); retained only as the direct physical continuation of v3's theophany, which IS retained on note (d)'s exception.

### Mic 1:5

> All this is for the transgression of Jacob and for the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what is the high place of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?

**Observation.** "All [H3605] this is for the transgression [H6588] of Jacob [H3290] and for the sins [H2403B] of the house [H1004M] of Israel [H3478]. What [H4310] is the transgression [H6588] of Jacob [H3290]? Is it not [H3808] Samaria [H8111]? And what [H4310] is the high place [H1116] of Judah [H3063G]? Is it not [H3808] Jerusalem [H3389]?"

**Operation 1 — the stated cause of the theophany: Jacob's transgression and Israel's sin.**
- **Action-type:** transgressed/sinned (the verse's first explicit naming of the guilt that grounds vv3-4).
- **Subject:** Jacob/the house of Israel — a national collective (note (c)), directly charged.
- **Operation:** a state — a condition of transgression/sin, named as the reason ("for," H9003) the preceding theophany occurs at all.
- **Source:** self — Jacob/Israel's own condition, not attributed to an outside cause.
- **Target:** n/a directly within this clause (the transgression's effects are the theophany itself, already described).

**Operation 2 — the rhetorical identification: Jacob's transgression IS Samaria; Judah's high place IS Jerusalem.**
- **Action-type:** identified/named (a rhetorical question-and-answer collapsing a nation's sin into its own capital city).
- **Subject:** Jacob/Israel, identified with Samaria (its capital); Judah, identified with Jerusalem (its capital and, strikingly, named as Judah's own "high place" — an idolatrous-worship term applied to the very city housing the LORD's own temple, v2).
- **Operation:** a state — a rhetorical equation, not a new act; the guilt named in Operation 1 is here located specifically in each kingdom's own capital.
- **Source:** self — again Jacob/Israel's and Judah's own condition, not externally caused.
- **Target:** n/a — reflexive, a nation identified with its own city.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Jacob/house of Israel and Judah — both national collectives, given here their first stated interior content (transgression, sin) in the chapter.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, via direct declarative statement and rhetorical Q&A.
- Q4: Source of both nations' guilt = self, explicit; no external cause named.
- Q5: N/A directly — the guilt is stated as a condition, not an act with an external target within this verse.
- Q6: State throughout (a condition of transgression/sin, then its rhetorical identification with a place).
- Q7: **Major linkage.** This verse directly answers v2's open "you" (the courtroom's accused is now named: Jacob/Israel, Judah) and directly grounds v3-4's theophany (the "for" clause states its cause) and vv6-7's coming verdict (Samaria, named here, is the specific target of v6).
- Q8: Jacob/house of Israel, Judah — both national collectives, each identified with a single city.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the specific content of the transgression/sin (what, exactly, Jacob and Judah did) is not detailed here — resolved partially by v7's harlotry/idolatry charge.
- Q11: transgressed/sinned (Operation 1); identified (Operation 2, the city-equation).

**Decision.** Retain both operations. The city-equation (Samaria = Jacob's transgression; Jerusalem = Judah's high place) is retained as the verse's structurally central move, directly grounding everything from v6 onward.

### Mic 1:6

> Therefore I will make Samaria a heap in the open country, a place for planting vineyards, and I will pour down her stones into the valley and uncover her foundations.

**Observation.** "Therefore I will make [H7760A] Samaria [H8111] a heap [H5856] in the open country [H7704G], a place for planting [H4302] vineyards [H3754]; and I will pour down [H5064] her stones [H0068G] into the valley [H1516R] and uncover [H1540I] her foundations [H3247H]."

**Operation 1 — the LORD's declared demolition of Samaria.**
- **Action-type:** made-a-heap/poured-down/uncovered (a direct divine verdict, the specific fulfillment of v2's witness-declaration against the city named at v5).
- **Subject:** the LORD, speaking in first person ("I will make"); Samaria, the city addressed/described throughout, personified as "her."
- **Operation:** a movement — total architectural destruction: reduced to rubble, repurposed as open farmland, its building-stones tumbled into the valley, its very foundations exposed.
- **Source:** self — the LORD's own declared act, "therefore" (drawing the direct consequence from v5's charge).
- **Target:** Samaria — its stones, its foundations, specifically and totally.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Samaria — continuing as the addressed subject from v5, now the direct object of a specific, detailed verdict; no new interior content of Samaria's own is stated here (that comes at v7), only what will be done TO it.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, as direct first-person divine declaration.
- Q4: Source = the LORD, self, explicit, directly causally linked ("therefore") to v5's charge.
- Q5: Target = Samaria, its stones and foundations.
- Q6: Movement throughout (demolition, exposure).
- Q7: Direct linkage to v5 ("therefore" explicitly draws the consequence) and forward to v9 (the same judgment's "wound" spreading onward to Judah/Jerusalem).
- Q8: N/A this verse — Samaria addressed as one personified city/collective.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: made-a-heap/poured-down/uncovered.

**Decision.** Retain — the direct, specific verdict answering v2's witness-declaration and v5's charge.

### Mic 1:7

> All her carved images shall be beaten to pieces, all her wages shall be burned with fire, and all her idols I will lay waste, for from the fee of a prostitute she gathered them, and to the fee of a prostitute they shall return.

**Observation.** "All [H3605] her carved images [H6456] shall be beaten to pieces [H3807], all [H3605] her wages [H0868] shall be burned [H8313] with fire [H0784]; and all [H3605] her idols [H6091] I will lay waste [H7760A], for from the fee [H0868] of a prostitute [H2181] she gathered [H6908] them, and to the fee [H0868] of a prostitute [H2181] they shall return [H7725G]."

**Operation 1 — the destruction of Samaria's idols, and the naming of her own harlotry.**
- **Action-type:** beaten/burned/laid-waste (continuing v6's demolition, now specifically targeting cultic objects); gathered/returned (Samaria's own past act, now stated as the reason).
- **Subject:** Samaria — this verse's first STATED interior content belonging to the city itself (not merely a description of what will happen to it, as in v6): "she gathered them," an active, self-attributed past act, framed as spiritual harlotry (H2181, zanah — the same verb used elsewhere in the prophetic corpus for covenant-unfaithfulness).
- **Operation:** a movement — idols destroyed by an outside agent (grammatically unstated within this verse, continuing v6's "I"); and a state/act genuinely Samaria's own — gathering wealth from prostitution-wages to fund idol-making, wealth now stated to "return" to that same source (i.e., carried off as plunder, to be reused as literal or figurative harlotry-wages elsewhere).
- **Source:** the LORD (idol destruction, continuing v6's "I"); Samaria's own harlotry (the idols' origin, self-attributed, explicit — a real instance of the text sourcing an interior/moral condition to the subject itself, not merely describing what is done to it).
- **Target:** the idols themselves (destruction); n/a directly for the harlotry clause (reflexive, describing Samaria's own past conduct).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Samaria — given here its first directly self-attributed interior content: unfaithfulness, described via the harlotry/wages metaphor. A genuine, explicit statement of moral/spiritual condition, not merely of coming fate.
- Q3: Stated explicitly — "for... she gathered them" directly attributes the act and its motive to Samaria itself.
- Q4: Source of the idol-destruction = the LORD, continuing v6. Source of the original idol-wealth = Samaria's own harlotry, explicitly self-attributed — an unusually direct case (compare Obad 3's parallel construction) of the text sourcing an interior/moral condition to the subject's own conduct rather than an external cause.
- Q5: Target = the idols (destruction); reflexive (the harlotry clause, describing Samaria's own past).
- Q6: Movement (destruction) and state/act (the harlotry, past and recurring).
- Q7: Direct linkage to v5 (resolving what, specifically, Jacob's "transgression" consisted of — idolatry funded by, and now returning to, harlotry) and to v6 (continuing the same demolition).
- Q8: N/A — Samaria addressed as one personified entity.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the specific historical mechanism of "returning to the fee of a prostitute" (plunder reused elsewhere, or a figurative recycling of ill-gotten wealth) is not further detailed.
- Q11: beaten/burned/laid-waste (idols); gathered/returned (Samaria's own harlotry).

**Decision.** Retain both operations. Samaria's own self-attributed harlotry is retained as the chapter's first directly-stated moral/interior content belonging to the guilty party itself, resolving v5's bare "transgression" into a specific charge.

### Mic 1:8

> For this I will lament and wail; I will go stripped and naked; I will make lamentation like the jackals, and mourning like the ostriches.

**Observation.** "For this I will lament [H5594] and wail [H3213]; I will go [H1980G] stripped [H7758] and naked [H6174]; I will make [H6213H] lamentation [H4553] like the jackals [H8577A], and mourning [H0060] like the ostriches [H1323G/H3284]."

**Operation 1 — Micah's own first-person grief at the judgment he has just pronounced.**
- **Action-type:** lamented/wailed/went-naked/mourned (a vivid, sustained first-person emotional and ritual response — the chapter's clearest, most direct stated human interior content).
- **Subject:** Micah — the prophet himself, returning to first person from v1's frame, now giving his own reaction rather than reporting the LORD's.
- **Operation:** a state — genuine, stated grief, enacted through mourning ritual (going stripped/naked, a recognised ancient mourning practice) and animal-cry imagery (jackals, ostriches — creatures of desolate, wild places, evoking both the sound and the setting of the coming devastation).
- **Source:** self — Micah's own response, directly caused by "this" (the judgment just pronounced against Samaria, and by extension its reach toward Judah, made explicit at v9).
- **Target:** n/a directly — reflexive, Micah's own state and enacted mourning; implicitly modelling, for the reader, the appropriate response to the devastation described.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Micah — the chapter's most directly and vividly stated human interior: real, personal grief, not inferred from an outward act alone but explicitly named ("I will lament and wail").
- Q3: Stated explicitly, in first person, four verbs deep.
- Q4: Source = Micah himself, self, explicit; the enabling cause = "this," the judgment just pronounced (vv6-7), Part B.5's state-vs-enablement distinction cleanly illustrated: Micah's grief is his own, but its cause is named.
- Q5: N/A directly — reflexive; no further external target within this verse.
- Q6: State (grief) enacted through movement (going naked, making lamentation).
- Q7: Direct linkage back to vv6-7 (Micah's grief is the stated response to the very verdict just pronounced) and forward to v9 (the wound's reach into Judah, his own kingdom, sharpening the grief's stakes).
- Q8: N/A — Micah addressed as an individual.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: lamented/wailed/went-naked/mourned.

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's single clearest instance of directly stated human inner-being content, positioned deliberately between the divine verdict against Samaria (vv6-7) and its spread into Judah (v9).

### Mic 1:9

> For her wound is incurable, and it has come to Judah; it has reached to the gate of my people, to Jerusalem.

**Observation.** "For her wound [H4347] is incurable [H0605], and it has come [H0935G] to Judah [H3063G]; it has reached [H5060] to the gate [H8179G] of my people [H5971A], to Jerusalem [H3389]."

**Operation 1 — Samaria's wound spreading to Judah and Jerusalem.**
- **Action-type:** spread/reached (the judgment's contagion, extending the demolition of vv6-7 beyond its original target).
- **Subject:** "her wound" (Samaria's own affliction, personified as a moving agent in its own right); "my people" — the LORD's own first-person possessive naming of Judah/Jerusalem, directly paralleling the divine-possessive pattern already observed in this study's own record (Joel 1:6-7's "my land, my vine, my fig tree"; Joel 3:2's "my people, my heritage, my land"; Obad 13's "my people," 16's "my holy mountain").
- **Operation:** a movement — the wound itself travels, reaching as far as Jerusalem's own gate.
- **Source:** Samaria's own incurable condition (continuing directly from vv6-7), not a newly-introduced agent.
- **Target:** Judah; specifically, "the gate of my people," Jerusalem — the LORD's own possession, raising the moral stakes of what began as Samaria's own judgment.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The wound itself is not a human candidate, but its target ("my people," Jerusalem) is — a national collective, now drawn directly into a judgment that began against a different kingdom's capital.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, as direct narrated fact.
- Q4: Source = Samaria's own condition, continuing vv6-7, self, not externally introduced; the wound's reach into Judah is stated as consequence, not a fresh divine act restated within this verse.
- Q5: Target = Judah; "the gate of my people," Jerusalem.
- Q6: Movement (the wound's spread).
- Q7: **Direct linkage to vv6-7** (the same judgment, extending its reach) and **forward to the whole of vv10-16** (which now unfolds as this wound's specific, town-by-town progress through Judah toward Jerusalem itself).
- Q8: N/A this verse for "my people" as addressed collective (treated at scale in the coming verses' individual towns).
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: spread/reached.

**Decision.** Retain — the structural hinge of the chapter, turning the oracle from Samaria alone toward the sequence of Judahite towns that follows.

### Mic 1:10

> Tell it not in Gath; weep not at all; in Beth-le-aphrah roll yourselves in the dust.

**Observation.** "Tell it not [H0408/H5046] in Gath [H1661]; weep not [H0408/H1058] at all [H1058]; in Beth-le-aphrah [H1036] roll yourselves [H6428] in the dust [H6083]."

**Operation 1 — the opening pair of the town-by-town wordplay lament: Gath and Beth-le-aphrah.**
- **Action-type:** told/wept/rolled-in-dust (three commanded/prohibited mourning responses, opening the chapter's distinct sub-genre — a chain of laments, each keyed to a town's own name).
- **Subject:** an unnamed addressee at Gath (prohibited from telling — a Philistine city, outside Judah, where the news must not spread lest Judah's enemies gloat); "Beth-le-aphrah" ("house of dust," H1036 — its own name sharing the same root as "dust," H6083, used explicitly in the same clause's command to roll in it) — a directly textually-anchored wordplay, the shared root visible in this verse's own vocabulary, not asserted from outside knowledge.
- **Operation:** a movement — a prohibition (do not tell, do not weep) paired with a commanded mourning-ritual (rolling in dust) whose form is drawn directly from the town's own name.
- **Source:** self — the addressees' own commanded/prohibited response.
- **Target:** n/a directly — reflexive mourning behaviour.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The addressees at Gath and Beth-le-aphrah — unnamed collectives (note (c)), given directly commanded emotional/ritual responses; a genuinely stated (if terse) interior directive.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, via direct imperative/prohibition.
- Q4: Source = the addressees' own commanded response; enabled/caused by the wound of v9, continuing.
- Q5: N/A directly — reflexive.
- Q6: Movement (rolling in dust); state (the prohibition against telling/weeping).
- Q7: Opens the vv10-16 wordplay chain — Beth-le-aphrah's own name-pun is the clearest, most directly textually-confirmed instance in the whole sequence (see insufficiencies register for the remaining towns, where the pun is traditionally recognised but not independently confirmed by this base extract's own lexicon data).
- Q8: Both addressees are unnamed town-collectives, treated as single units.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the reason telling-not is commanded at Gath specifically (traditionally, a Philistine city where such news would provoke enemy gloating, echoing 2Sam 1:20's identical phrase) is not supplied by this base extract's own data — named as insufficiency, not imported from outside knowledge.
- Q11: told/wept/rolled-in-dust.

**Decision.** Retain — the opening instance of the chapter's wordplay-lament device, with Beth-le-aphrah/dust standing as the one pun directly confirmed by this verse's own shared vocabulary.

### Mic 1:11

**Observation.** "Pass on your way [H5674A], inhabitants [H3427] of Shaphir [H8208], in nakedness [H6181] and shame [H1322]; the inhabitants [H3427] of Zaanan [H6630] do not [H3808] come out [H3318G]; the lamentation [H4553] of Beth-ezel [H1018] shall take [H3947G] away from you its standing place [H5979]."

**Operation 1 — three further town-collectives, each given a distinct, commanded or reported fate.**
- **Action-type:** passed-on/stayed-in/lost-standing-place (three distinct operations chained by the same wordplay device).
- **Subject:** "the inhabitants of Shaphir" (a human collective, note (c)); "the inhabitants of Zaanan" (likewise); "Beth-ezel" (a town whose own "lamentation" is personified as the agent taking away its standing place — an unusual construction, the town's own grief becoming what dispossesses it).
- **Operation:** a movement — Shaphir's inhabitants commanded to go into exile-like nakedness and shame; Zaanan's inhabitants stated (not commanded) to stay shut in, not daring to come out; Beth-ezel's own lamentation stated to remove its "standing place" (a term for a base, foothold, or support).
- **Source:** self (each town's own commanded/stated response), continuing the judgment inaugurated at vv6-9.
- **Target:** n/a directly — each town's own condition, reflexively described.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: All three town-collectives — genuine, stated (if terse) interior/behavioural content: shame (Shaphir), fear/withdrawal (Zaanan, implied by staying in rather than a stated emotion), grief (Beth-ezel's own "lamentation," explicitly named).
- Q3: Stated explicitly for all three, via command (Shaphir), direct report (Zaanan), and direct declarative (Beth-ezel).
- Q4: Source = each town's own condition/response, continuing the wound of v9; no new external agent introduced within this verse.
- Q5: N/A directly — each clause reflexive to its own town.
- Q6: Movement (Shaphir's commanded passing-on in shame; Beth-ezel's loss of standing) and state (Zaanan's staying-in).
- Q7: Continues the vv10-16 wordplay chain; the traditional puns on Shaphir ("beautiful," ironically now shamed), Zaanan (resembling "go out," now unable to), and Beth-ezel ("house of taking away," now itself losing its own footing) are widely recognised in this passage's reading but are NOT independently confirmed by this base extract's own lexicon data (no etymological gloss is supplied for any of the three names) — named as insufficiency, not asserted as fact.
- Q8: All three subjects are town-collectives, treated as single units (note (c)).
- Q9: Insufficient — the specific phonetic/etymological basis for each pun is not supplied by this base extract; retained as widely-recognised structural reading of the passage, not as a confirmed data point.
- Q11: passed-on-in-shame (Shaphir); stayed-in (Zaanan); lost-standing-place (Beth-ezel).

**Decision.** Retain all three operations as continuing the wordplay-lament chain; the underlying puns themselves are flagged as traditional/unconfirmed by this base extract, per Part B.7.

### Mic 1:12

**Observation.** "For the inhabitants [H3427] of Maroth [H4796] wait anxiously [H2342K] for good [H2896B], because disaster [H7451B] has come down [H3381] from [H9006] the LORD [H3068G] to the gate [H8179G] of Jerusalem [H3389]."

**Operation 1 — Maroth's own anxious waiting, and the disaster's arrival from the LORD.**
- **Action-type:** waited-anxiously (a genuinely stated interior state — anxious hope); came-down (repeating v3-4's own action-type for the theophany's descent, now applied to "disaster" specifically).
- **Subject:** "the inhabitants of Maroth" (a human collective, note (c)), given a directly stated interior — anxious longing for a good outcome that will not come; the LORD, restated as the disaster's explicit source.
- **Operation:** a state — Maroth's own anxious hope (H2342K, the same root elsewhere covering writhing/travail, here in its "wait longingly" sense — a vivid, embodied anxiety, not mere passive waiting); a movement — the disaster's descent, using the identical verb (H3381, yarad) already used for the LORD's own theophanic "coming down" at v3-4, an intra-chapter action-type recurrence.
- **Source:** Maroth's own hope (self); the disaster's source = the LORD, explicit, restated directly (not merely implied as in vv9-11).
- **Target:** n/a directly for Maroth's own hope (reflexive); "the gate of Jerusalem" for the disaster's arrival.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Maroth's inhabitants — genuinely stated interior content: anxious hope for a good outcome, explicitly named, not merely inferred from an outward act.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, both the hope and its frustration (disaster, not good, actually arrives).
- Q4: Source of Maroth's hope = self; source of the disaster = the LORD, explicit, restated.
- Q5: Target = Jerusalem's own gate — continuing v9's identical destination ("the gate of my people, to Jerusalem"), now reached by name a second time.
- Q6: State (anxious hope) and movement (the disaster's descent).
- Q7: **Direct linkage to v3-4** — "come down" (H3381) recurs here for the disaster's own arrival, the same action-type used for the LORD's theophanic descent, an intra-divine-action recurrence within the chapter (not a Q12 human-vs-divine mirror, since both instances are the LORD's own operation, not a human one set against it). Direct linkage to v9 (both reach "the gate of Jerusalem").
- Q8: "The inhabitants of Maroth" — a town-collective, treated as one unit.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the traditional pun on Maroth (resembling "bitter," מַר) is not confirmed by this base extract's own data — named as insufficiency, not asserted.
- Q11: waited-anxiously (Maroth); came-down (the disaster, from the LORD).

**Decision.** Retain — Maroth's own stated anxious hope, directly frustrated by the LORD's own disaster, reaching Jerusalem's gate a second time (compare v9).

### Mic 1:13

> Harness the steeds to the chariots, inhabitants of Lachish; it was the beginning of sin to the daughter of Zion, for in you were found the transgressions of Israel.

**Observation.** "Harness [H7573] the steeds [H7409] to the chariots [H4818], inhabitants [H3427] of Lachish [H3923]; it [H1931] was the beginning [H7225G] of sin [H2403B] to the daughter [H1323G] of Zion [H6726], for in you were found [H4672] the transgressions [H6588] of Israel [H3478]."

**Operation 1 — Lachish commanded to harness for flight/war, and directly charged as the origin-point of Zion's sin.**
- **Action-type:** harnessed (a commanded act, likely urgent flight or military mobilisation); was-the-beginning-of/were-found (a direct, explicit charge of guilt).
- **Subject:** "the inhabitants of Lachish" (a human collective, note (c)); "the daughter of Zion" (Jerusalem, personified, here named as the recipient of a sin that BEGAN specifically at Lachish.
- **Operation:** a movement — the commanded harnessing itself; a state — Lachish directly and explicitly named as where "the transgressions of Israel" were "found," i.e., where Judah's own guilt is traced to a specific origin, not merely a general charge as at v5.
- **Source:** self (Lachish's own commanded act); Lachish's own conduct, explicitly self-attributed as the SOURCE of Zion's sin — a direct, unusually specific instance of the text naming exactly where a nation's guilt originated, continuing v7's pattern of self-attributed moral content.
- **Target:** "the daughter of Zion" — directly named as having received/inherited sin FROM Lachish, a striking city-to-city transmission of guilt.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Lachish's inhabitants — given here the chapter's most explicit, most specific charge of originating guilt (not merely bearing it, as elsewhere in vv10-16).
- Q3: Stated explicitly, via direct declarative ("it was the beginning of sin... for in you were found").
- Q4: Source = Lachish's own conduct, self, explicit — directly, unusually specifically named.
- Q5: Target = "the daughter of Zion" — Jerusalem, receiving/inheriting this originating guilt.
- Q6: Movement (harnessing) and state (the guilt-transmission).
- Q7: **Major linkage** — directly resolves part of v5's general charge ("the transgressions of Israel... in you") by locating a specific origin-point (Lachish) for Zion's own sin, tightening the chain from national guilt (v5) through a specific town (v13) to the mother-city herself (vv13, 16).
- Q8: "The inhabitants of Lachish" — a town-collective, treated as one unit.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; WHAT specifically originated at Lachish (chariot-warfare associated with royal military build-up, on one traditional reading) is not detailed by this base extract's own data — named as insufficiency. The traditional pun on Lachish (resembling "team of horses," רֶכֶשׁ) is likewise not confirmed by this extract's own lexicon.
- Q11: harnessed (commanded act); was-the-beginning-of/were-found (the guilt-charge).

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's most specific, explicitly self-attributed charge of originating guilt, directly tightening v5's general national charge into a named town-to-capital transmission.

### Mic 1:14

> Therefore you shall give parting gifts to Moresheth-gath; the houses of Achzib shall be a deceitful thing to the kings of Israel.

**Observation.** "Therefore [H3651C] you shall give [H5414G] parting gifts [H7964] to Moresheth-gath [H4182]; the houses [H1004B] of Achzib [H0392G] shall be a deceitful thing [H0391] to the kings [H4428G] of Israel [H3478]."

**Operation 1 — the commanded relinquishing of Moresheth-gath, and Achzib's own stated unreliability.**
- **Action-type:** gave-parting-gifts (a commanded act of relinquishment, likened to the dowry/farewell-gift given when a daughter leaves her father's house in marriage — the addressed party commanded to "give away" its own possession); deceived (a stated, explicit charge against Achzib).
- **Subject:** an unnamed addressee (likely Judah/Jerusalem, continuing the address from v13) commanded to give up Moresheth-gath — Micah's own hometown (directly named at v1, "Micah of Moresheth"), a notable personal linkage: the prophet's own native town is caught up in the very judgment he pronounces; "the houses of Achzib" — a town whose own name (traditionally resembling "deception," כָּזָב) is here directly, explicitly called "a deceitful thing" — one of the clearest wordplay instances in the chapter, since the SAME root idea (deceit) is both the town's traditional name-sense and its stated verdict, though the extract's own lexicon does not itself gloss the name's etymology (named as insufficiency below).
- **Operation:** a movement — Moresheth-gath relinquished, given away; a state — Achzib itself declared unreliable, a false hope to the very kings who might look to it.
- **Source:** self (the commanded relinquishment); Achzib's own nature, self-attributed as deceptive.
- **Target:** Moresheth-gath (given away); "the kings of Israel," deceived by Achzib.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The unnamed addressee (Judah/Zion, continuing v13) — commanded to an act of loss; "the kings of Israel" — named as the ones deceived, a human party distinct from the towns themselves.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, via command and direct declarative charge.
- Q4: Source = the addressee's own commanded act (Moresheth-gath); Achzib's own nature, self-attributed, explicit.
- Q5: Target = Moresheth-gath (given away); the kings of Israel (deceived).
- Q6: Movement (the relinquishment) and state (Achzib's declared unreliability).
- Q7: **Personal linkage, worth carrying forward as an emergent question**: Moresheth-gath is Micah's own home town (v1), directly named among the towns being lamented/lost — the prophet is not a detached observer of this judgment but personally implicated in it.
- Q8: "The kings of Israel" — a ruling-class collective, distinct from the town-inhabitant collectives addressed elsewhere in vv10-16.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the precise nature of the "parting gift" custom, and the specific incident behind "the kings of Israel" being deceived by Achzib, are not detailed by this base extract — named as insufficiency.
- Q11: gave-parting-gifts (Moresheth-gath); deceived (Achzib).

**Decision.** Retain both operations. Moresheth-gath's inclusion is flagged as a significant personal linkage for Micah himself, carried forward to the emergent-questions log.

### Mic 1:15

**Operation 1 — the LORD's declared bringing of a conqueror against Mareshah, and Israel's glory reduced to Adullam.**
- **Action-type:** brought (a direct divine act, first-person, restating the LORD as the acting agent after several verses of unattributed passive/commanded constructions); came/reduced-to (Israel's own "glory" now stated to arrive, ironically, at a hiding-place).

- **Operation:** a movement — a conqueror brought against Mareshah; Israel's own "glory" reduced to seeking refuge at a byword for hiding and diminishment.
- **Source:** self — the LORD, explicit, restated directly.

### Mic 1:16

> Make yourselves bald and cut off your hair, for the children of your delight; make yourselves as bald as the eagle, for they shall go from you into exile.

**Observation.** "Make yourselves bald [H7139] and cut off [H1494] your hair, for [H5921A] the children [H1121A] of your delight [H8588]; make yourselves as bald [H7337/H7144] as [H9004] the eagle [H5404], for [H3588A] they shall go [H1540K] from you into exile."

**Operation 1 — the commanded mourning-ritual for the exile of one's own beloved children.**
- **Action-type:** made-bald/cut-off-hair (a commanded, ritual act of extreme mourning, closing the chapter's wordplay-lament chain with a direct, un-punned command addressed to the personified mother-city herself, continuing v13's "daughter of Zion").
- **Subject:** the addressed mother-city (Zion/Judah, personified as a grieving parent, continuing from v13); "the children of your delight" — her own beloved offspring, directly named as the object of her grief.
- **Operation:** a state — commanded mourning (baldness, an ancient mourning practice, here doubled — "bald... and cut off," then "bald as the eagle," an intensifying repetition); a movement — the children's own departure, explicitly named as exile.
- **Source:** self (the commanded mourning-response); the exile's cause continues the whole chapter's judgment, not restated as a fresh agent within this verse.
- **Target:** n/a directly for the mourning (reflexive); the children themselves, who "go... into exile."

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The addressed mother-city — a genuinely stated, deeply personal interior content: parental grief, directly named, closing the chapter on its most intimate register yet ("the children of your delight" — not merely "the people" but a term of tender endearment). "The children" themselves — a human collective (note (c)), given a stated fate (exile) but no interior of their own.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, via direct command and direct declarative ("for they shall go... into exile").
- Q4: Source of the mourning = self, commanded; source of the exile = continuing the whole chapter's judgment (the LORD's own verdict, vv6-15), not restated explicitly here.
- Q5: Target = n/a for the mourning itself; the children, who depart into exile.
- Q6: State (mourning) and movement (the children's departure).
- Q7: **Closing linkage, chapter-bracketing.** The chapter opened with Micah's OWN grief (v8, "I will lament... I will go stripped and naked") and closes with the mother-city commanded to an equivalent, even more intimate grief (baldness, for her own children) — the prophet's personal mourning at the chapter's start modelling the whole nation's own mourning at its close. Also directly continues v13's "daughter of Zion" address and v9's structural movement from Samaria's wound toward Jerusalem/Judah's own household.
- Q8: "The children of your delight" — a collective, but framed with unusually personal, affectionate language (note (c) reshaped: not a bare demographic collective but a beloved family unit).
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the traditional pun on "bald... as the eagle" (the griffon-vulture's naturally bald head/neck, a stock image for mourning) is a natural-history observation the base extract's own gloss ("eagle, vulture, griffon-vulture") does support directly, unlike the town-name puns elsewhere in this passage.
- Q11: made-bald/cut-off-hair (the mourning); went-into-exile (the children).

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's closing operation, bracketing back to Micah's own opening grief (v8) and completing the movement from Samaria's wound (v9) to Judah's own household loss.

## Passage-level linkages (Q7)

1. **The theophany-to-verdict chain**: vv3-4 (the LORD's cosmic descent) → v5 (its stated cause: Jacob/Judah's transgression, identified with Samaria/Jerusalem) → vv6-7 (Samaria's specific verdict) — the whole opening movement of the chapter, cause and effect made explicit rather than merely juxtaposed.
2. **The wound's southward progress**: v6-7 (Samaria's demolition) → v9 (the wound reaching Judah, "to the gate of my people, to Jerusalem") → vv10-16 (a chain of Judahite towns, each individually named and afflicted, converging on Jerusalem/Zion herself) — the whole second half of the chapter is this single wound's continued advance, town by town.
3. **The wordplay-lament chain (vv10-16)**: seven towns in sequence (Gath, Beth-le-aphrah, Shaphir, Zaanan, Beth-ezel, Maroth, Lachish, Moresheth-gath, Achzib, Mareshah, Adullam — eleven named locations across seven verses), each given a fate keyed, traditionally, to a pun on its own name; only Beth-le-aphrah's pun (v10, "house of dust"/"roll in the dust") is directly confirmed by this base extract's own shared vocabulary — the rest are widely-recognised in the passage's traditional reading but not independently confirmed by the extract's own lexicon data (see insufficiencies register).
4. **Bracketing grief**: Micah's own first-person lament (v8, "I will lament and wail... go stripped and naked") is directly answered, structurally, by the mother-city's own commanded lament at the chapter's close (v16, "make yourselves bald... for the children of your delight") — the prophet's personal grief modelling the whole nation's own.
5. **The "come down" (H3381, yarad) recurrence**: the LORD's own theophanic descent (v3-4) and the disaster's arrival at Maroth (v12) share the identical verb — an intra-divine action-type recurrence within one chapter, not a Q12 human-vs-divine mirror (both instances belong to the LORD's own action), but worth tracking as a recurring divine-action vocabulary item.
6. **The divine-possessive pattern**: "my people" (v9) continues the same framing already observed in Joel (1:6-7, 3:2) and Obadiah (13, 16) — a recurring device across the prophetic books read so far in this study, now a third/fourth instance.
7. **Micah's own personal stake**: Moresheth-gath (v14), Micah's own home town (named at v1, "Micah of Moresheth"), appears among the very towns being lamented — the prophet is not a detached observer but personally implicated in the judgment he pronounces (compare, though differently shaped, Jonah's own personal entanglement in his book's outcome).
8. **Guilt's transmission, town to capital**: v5's general national charge ("the transgressions of Israel") is progressively specified — v7 (Samaria's own self-attributed harlotry), v13 (Lachish explicitly named as "the beginning of sin" for "the daughter of Zion," guilt shown moving FROM a town TO the capital, the reverse direction of the wound's own southward spread).
9. **Reversal/irony as a structuring device**: v2's summoned "peoples" possibly also being the accused (an open fork); v13's guilt flowing the "wrong" direction (town to capital); v15's national "glory" arriving, ironically, at Adullam, a byword for hiding rather than triumph.

## Insufficiencies register

- The identity of "you" in v2's "let the Lord GOD be a witness against you" is not resolved within the verse itself — whether identical to the just-summoned "peoples" or a distinct, not-yet-named party — carried forward as an interpretive fork (Part B.9), not settled here.
- The etymological/phonetic basis for the wordplay puns traditionally read at Gath (v10, "tell"), Shaphir (v11, "beautiful"), Zaanan (v11, "go out"), Beth-ezel (v11, "taking away"), Maroth (v12, "bitter"), Lachish (v13, "team of horses"), Achzib (v14, "deception"), and Mareshah (v15, "conqueror/heir") is widely recognised in traditional reading of this passage but is **not confirmed by this base extract's own lexicon data** — only Beth-le-aphrah/dust (v10) and the eagle's natural baldness (v16) are directly supported by the extract's own glosses. Named as insufficiency throughout, per Part B.7, not imported from outside scholarly knowledge.
- The specific historical campaign behind the town-by-town devastation of vv10-15 (traditionally associated with an Assyrian invasion of Judah) is not named or dated within this base extract's own data.
- What, specifically, "the beginning of sin" originating at Lachish (v13) consisted of is not detailed by this base extract.
- The precise custom behind "parting gifts" (v14, likened to a dowry/farewell gift) is not detailed within this base extract.
- The specific incident behind "the kings of Israel" being deceived by Achzib (v14) is not named.

## Emergent questions log (filed against this passage — not merged across passages; resolved, if at all, at the whole-book read)

- **EQ1.** The divine-possessive "my people" (v9) is now the third-or-fourth instance of this framing observed across this study's prophetic reading so far (Joel 1:6-7, 3:2; Obadiah 13, 16). Worth weighing together, once more of the Twelve are read, as a genuine recurring device rather than a coincidence of individual books.
- **EQ2.** v2's dual-role addressee (the summoned "peoples," possibly also the accused "you" of the same verse) is a genuinely open interpretive fork this passage does not itself resolve. Watch for whether this summons-that-may-also-be-an-accusation pattern recurs elsewhere in the corpus.
- **EQ3.** The wordplay-lament sub-genre of vv10-16 (a chain of town-by-town name-puns) is a distinct literary device not yet seen in Joel/Jonah/Obadiah. Worth flagging as a new device-category for cross-book tracking once more of the Twelve (and any other Hebrew poetic/prophetic material using paronomasia) are read — and worth returning to with fuller lexical/etymological data than this base extract currently supplies, if that data is ever added.
- **EQ4.** Micah's own hometown (Moresheth-gath, v14) appearing within the very list of towns being lamented raises a genuine question about the prophet's own personal stake in his oracles, worth comparing — once more prophetic books are read — against Jonah's own different, but comparably personal, entanglement in his book's outcome.
- **EQ5.** The "come down" (H3381) recurrence between the LORD's own theophany (v3-4) and the disaster's arrival at Maroth (v12) — within a single chapter — raises the question of whether this verb functions as a stock item for divine intervention across the corpus; worth tracking forward.

## Open decisions / next steps

- Whether the vv10-16 wordplay-lament unit should be tagged going forward as its own recognised sub-passage type in this method's own terms (distinct from ordinary narrative or direct divine-speech verses) is left open — a resourcing/formalisation question in the same category as Part B.10's caution against premature classification, not decided here.
- The historical/geographical specifics behind vv10-15 remain unconfirmed by this base extract; if ever needed for a fuller reading, would require explicitly-sourced external historical-geographical data, not assumed from memory.
- Next: Mic 2 (chapter 2 of 7, per the researcher's instruction that each chapter is processed as its own oracle-unit in sequence). `report.whole_book_read` remains the natural step once all 7 chapters are debated, not run per-chapter, matching Daniel/Jonah/Joel/Obadiah's own established sequence.
